title: Best WiFi Dehumidifier (2026): Smart, App-Controlled Picks
h1: The Best Wi-Fi Dehumidifiers: Smart Picks You Can Check From Your Phone
dek: An app alert is only useful if someone can act on it — or if the dehumidifier can drain itself. These smart picks get both halves right.
description: The best WiFi dehumidifier for 2026: smart, app-controlled picks with Alexa or Google support, tank alerts and built-in pumps for spaces you rarely visit.
intro: A **dehumidifier with Wi-Fi** lets you check humidity, change the target and get a tank-full or fault alert from your phone. That sounds like a gimmick until you think about where dehumidifiers live: basements you visit weekly, crawl spaces you never enter, and storage rooms nobody walks past.

Here’s the catch the marketing skips. An alert doesn’t empty a bucket. With the average homeowners insurance claim for water damage running close to **$14,000**, the smart features matter most when they’re paired with a pump or continuous drain — so the unit can handle the water whether or not you see the notification.
We ranked the best smart dehumidifiers by how good they are as dehumidifiers first, then by how useful their apps and drainage are for the space you’re putting them in.
topPicksLead: For most homes, the **Midea Cube 50** is the best Wi-Fi dehumidifier: an efficient, well-designed machine with app, Alexa and Google control.

products.name: Midea Cube 50-Pint Smart Dehumidifier (MAD50S1QWT)
pros: Midea Air app plus Alexa and Google Assistant
products.whyWeLoveIt: It isn’t an average dehumidifier padded out with an app — it’s one of the best 50-pint machines available that also happens to be connected, so you don’t trade performance for convenience.
products.performance: Independent bench testing recorded a 512-watt draw at 50% humidity, the lowest among the 50-pint units in that test, and Midea rates coverage up to 4,500 sq ft. The reservoir in the base holds about 34 pints, nearly triple a typical bucket, so even without a hose you empty it far less often. The app lets you set an exact humidity target and check tank status remotely.
products.notes: See the full lineup in our [best Midea dehumidifier](/best/best-midea-dehumidifier/) guide.

products.name: hOmeLabs 50-Pint Wi-Fi Dehumidifier with Pump (HME1003)
pros: App shows live humidity and tank status
products.whyWeLoveIt: Because it pumps water out on its own, the tank-full alert almost never matters. That turns the app into a handy status check instead of the only thing standing between you and an overflow.
products.performance: It’s a 50-pint-class compressor unit with an integrated condensate pump, so it can send water up to a sink or out a window from a basement without a floor drain. The app is useful for confirming a basement you rarely visit is staying under 50%. Compare it with other self-draining models in our [best dehumidifier with pump](/best/best-dehumidifier-with-pump/) roundup.

products.name: Frigidaire 70-Pint Smart Dehumidifier (FGAC7044U1)
pros: Familiar app if you own other Frigidaire appliances
products.whyWeLoveIt: When 50 pints won’t cut it — a big basement or an open floor plan — this Frigidaire adds real capacity while keeping app and voice control.
products.performance: It’s rated at 70 pints a day under the current DOE 2019 test, which is a genuine large-space rating. Drainage is by bucket or gravity hose, so if you rely on the app, make sure tank-full alerts are switched on. For other high-capacity options, see our [best 70-pint dehumidifier](/best/best-70-pint-dehumidifier/) guide.

products.name: AlorAir Sentinel HDi65S Wi-Fi Crawl Space Dehumidifier
pros: Built-in pump with 19.6 feet of lift
App confirms humidity without opening the hatch
products.whyWeLoveIt: This is where Wi-Fi earns its keep. Nobody checks a crawl space or server room in person, and pairing remote monitoring with a real pump means nothing needs emptying even if you never open the app.
products.performance: AlorAir rates it at 120 pints a day at saturation and 55 pints under AHAM conditions. Its pump lifts water 19.6 feet, enough to get out of most crawl spaces with no floor drain. Auto-defrost keeps it running in cool, unconditioned spaces that would freeze up a standard compressor unit.
products.notes: Compare the rest of the Sentinel range in our [crawl space dehumidifier](/best/best-crawl-space-dehumidifier/) picks.

products.name: Aprilaire E070W Wi-Fi Dehumidifier
pros: Healthy Air app for setpoints and alerts
products.whyWeLoveIt: If your dehumidifier will be tucked into a crawl space or tied into ductwork, this is the connected way to keep an eye on it without crawling in to check.
products.performance: It uses the same 70-pint hardware as the standard E070 with a Wi-Fi controller added. Aprilaire’s Healthy Air app handles remote setpoints, status and alerts, and the bucketless design means there’s no tank to fill. See our [Aprilaire guide](/best/best-aprilaire-dehumidifier/) for the full E-Series.

blocks.text: We don’t lab-test dehumidifiers. We compare DOE 2019 and AHAM capacity ratings, ENERGY STAR data, manuals and published independent bench results, then read owner reviews with a particular eye on the app: connection drops, missing alerts, and firmware updates that broke features.
We ranked each model on its core dehumidifying ability first, then on drainage, then on app and voice-assistant quality. A great app can’t rescue a mediocre machine.

sections.heading: What to look for in a smart Wi-Fi dehumidifier

items.label: Pump or continuous drain
items.text: This is what makes a remote unit truly hands-off. An alert alone still means a trip to empty the bucket.

items.label: Useful alerts
items.text: Tank-full, fault and humidity-out-of-range notifications matter more than remote on/off.

items.label: Voice support if you want it
items.text: Midea and Frigidaire work with Alexa; Aprilaire’s app doesn’t.

items.label: 2.4 GHz compatibility
items.text: Many appliance Wi-Fi modules connect only to 2.4 GHz networks. Check your router settings before setup.

items.label: The right size
items.text: Connectivity doesn’t change capacity. Use our [size guide](/guides/dehumidifier-size-guide/) to choose the right pint rating.

sections.heading: What a Wi-Fi dehumidifier app can and can’t do

items: **It alerts you; it doesn’t act for you.** Without a pump or hose, a tank-full notification still needs a person.
**It keeps working offline.** Every model here runs on its onboard humidistat if Wi-Fi drops; you just lose remote viewing and alerts.
**Voice support varies.** Check the specific model rather than assuming Alexa or Google works.
**It’s most valuable where you don’t go.** Basements, crawl spaces and server rooms benefit most.

blocks.text: Is a Wi-Fi crawl space dehumidifier worth it?

More than anywhere else. A crawl-space unit with a clogged drain or a failed pump gives no warning until something smells. An app alert is your early-warning system, and pairing it with a pump means the unit handles routine drainage on its own. Our [crawl space installation guide](/guides/crawl-space-dehumidifier-installation/) covers drain routing.

blocks.title: A brand that’s missing on purpose
blocks.text: Hisense sells plenty of connected TVs and fridges, but its current dehumidifiers don’t offer Wi-Fi or app control. See our [Hisense guide](/best/best-hisense-dehumidifier/) for what it does sell.

The **Midea Cube 50** is the best Wi-Fi dehumidifier for most people, with excellent efficiency, a big reservoir and Alexa and Google support. Choose the **hOmeLabs HME1003** for a pump at a lower price, the **Frigidaire FGAC7044U1** for 70-pint capacity, the **AlorAir HDi65S** for a crawl space or server room, and the **Aprilaire E070W** for a ducted install. Remember: the app tells you about a problem; a pump or drain is what prevents it.

faqs.q: What is the best smart Wi-Fi dehumidifier?
faqs.a: The Midea Cube 50 (MAD50S1QWT) for most homes, thanks to its efficiency, large reservoir and Midea Air app with Alexa and Google support. For a built-in pump at a lower price, the hOmeLabs HME1003 Wi-Fi is the value pick.

faqs.q: Is a dehumidifier with Wi-Fi worth it?
faqs.a: Yes, if it sits somewhere you don’t check daily. Tank-full and fault alerts can catch a problem before it becomes water damage. In a bedroom you walk through every day, the app is a nice extra rather than a necessity.

faqs.q: Does a Wi-Fi dehumidifier work if the internet goes down?
faqs.a: Yes. All the models here keep running on their built-in humidistat and controls without a connection. You only lose remote monitoring and alerts until Wi-Fi returns.

faqs.q: Do Wi-Fi dehumidifiers work with Alexa or Google Home?
faqs.a: Some do. The Midea Cube line supports Alexa and Google Assistant, and the Frigidaire FGAC7044U1 works with Alexa. Aprilaire’s Healthy Air app supports alerts and setpoints but not voice assistants.

faqs.q: Will a Wi-Fi dehumidifier’s app empty the tank for me?
faqs.a: No. The app can tell you the tank is full; only a built-in pump or a continuous drain hose removes the water automatically. For hands-off operation, choose a model like the hOmeLabs HME1003 or AlorAir HDi65S that pairs Wi-Fi with a pump.

faqs.q: What is the best Wi-Fi crawl space dehumidifier?
faqs.a: The AlorAir Sentinel HDi65S, which combines app monitoring with a built-in pump and auto-defrost for cool spaces. For a ducted or professionally installed system, the Aprilaire E070W is the connected option.

faqs.q: Why won’t my Wi-Fi dehumidifier connect to the app?
faqs.a: The most common cause is a 5 GHz-only network — many appliance Wi-Fi modules need 2.4 GHz. Also check that your phone is on the same network during setup, move the unit closer to the router, and confirm the app has location and Bluetooth permissions if it asks.
